# Arvato opens seventh Louisville facility, strength­ening its presence in key U.S. logistics hub 

As brands continue to expand across North America, many face increasing challenges in scaling their supply chains quickly, maintaining service levels and building resilience in an increasingly complex market environment. The new, wholly-owned site adds approximately 400,000 square feet of capacity, taking Arvato’s total Louisville footprint beyond four million square feet. Expected to create approximately 150 new jobs, the facility further strengthens Arvato’s ability to support growing fulfillment and distribution requirements for clients across North America.

# Grip is taking the guesswork out of shipping the cold stuff

 Riley Kaminer September 15, 2026 

For years, shipping perishable goods came with a costly rule of thumb: Send everything overnight, pack in as much coolant and insulation as possible, and hope for the best. Grip founder and CEO Juan Camilo Meisel thinks brands can be far more precise.

“This one box does require these four gel packs and this one service, but this other box, you can actually get away with two gel packs and this other shipment service that’s cheaper,” Meisel [pictured above] told Refresh Miami.

That focus has helped the Miami-based logistics and technology company grow 100% year over year for the past three years. Grip is nearing 200 employees and expanding the physical network behind its software. A new 150,000-square-foot facility in Reno was set to open Sept. 1, while the company has moved into a larger Michigan building and plans further growth in New Jersey and Florida. With five facilities, Grip expects to reach 80% of the U.S. population within 24 hours.

#### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

### Grip Expands West Coast Operations With New Reno Facility

 Press Release Date 09-01-2026

 

Grip's new 150,000-square-foot fulfillment facility in Sparks, Nevada.

New Northern Nevada hub extends the category leader's temperature-controlled fulfillment network across the West

RENO, NV, UNITED STATES, September 1, 2026 / EINPresswire.com/ -- Grip, the technology, fulfillment and logistics company revolutionizing the frozen and refrigerated e-commerce space, has opened a 150,000-square-foot facility creating more than 60 jobs in the Reno-Sparks area. The hub is the company's fifth nationwide and anchors its West Coast operations.

The facility places Grip within one-day ground shipping reach of approximately 60 million people across 11 Western states, including the Los Angeles, San Francisco, Seattle and Salt Lake City markets.
